findings.title: immediateDelete path never deletes/flags DB row
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true sends POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel to SendGrid and then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. Callers in handleNewBooking reschedule rely on this to clean up the old booking's reminders. The row stays with scheduled=true and the old referenceId. If the SendGrid call fails it is swallowed inside the function so there is no cron retry (cron only looks for cancelled=true), so the old scheduled email will still be sent after reschedule. Even on success it leaves stale rows until they age out via past-date deletion.

findings.title: One SendGrid failure aborts all cancellations and deletes
findings.body: The cron wraps the entire for-loop over remindersToCancel plus Promise.all of deletes in a single try/catch. If client.request cancel fails for one reminder, execution jumps to catch, skipping remaining reminders and skipping Promise.all for deletes already collected. One bad batch_id therefore leaves all other cancelled emails still scheduled in SendGrid, so they will still be sent.

findings.title: Cancel query missing method/scheduled/referenceId filters
findings.body: remindersToCancel selects where cancelled=true and scheduledDate within next hour, without filtering method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId NOT NULL. Any cancelled SMS row or unscheduled row with null referenceId would be sent to SendGrid POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends with batch_id null or a Twilio SID. That request fails and, combined with the single outer try/catch, blocks all valid email cancellations.

findings.title: Reminder cancels fired without await
findings.body: updatedBookings.forEach with nested workflowReminders.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises. Those functions do prisma update/delete and SendGrid/Twilio calls. The handler then proceeds to Promise.all of other deletes and returns success. In serverless the DB update marking cancelled=true may not complete, so the cron never sees it and the supposedly cancelled email/SMS is still sent. Same fire-and-forget pattern is repeated in handleNewBooking, bookings requestReschedule and workflows update/delete.

findings.title: Twilio failure prevents DB delete with no retry
findings.body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder does twilio.cancelSMS then prisma.workflowReminder.delete inside the same try. If cancelSMS throws, the delete is skipped and the error is only logged. Unlike email which has a deferred cancelled flag processed by cron, SMS has no retry path, so the row stays scheduled=true and the SMS will still be sent even though cancellation was requested.
